summary: Redwood AE+SE walked ArborHealth (CTO, ML/Platform/Security) through the Model Catalog UI and API patterns: selecting open models, reading performance profiles, compatibility matrices for quantization and hardware, and how benchmark results map to cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer is interested in Dedicated for throughput and data isolation; security team asked for SOC2 and KMS details. Agreed to run a 10k-query benchmark on Redwood Dedicated with suggested model candidates and share results in follow up.
transcript:
[15:30] Sofia Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we're gonna run through the model catalog demo, focus on how you pick open models, interpret benchmarks and the compatibility matrix.
[15:31] Maya Patel: Thanks, Sofia. Quick context: we have high throughput for notes ingestion, latency needs under 200ms p50 for critical flows, and security requirements - we need VPC + KMS.
[15:32] Daniel Lee: Got it. I'll show both the Console view and a quick API call pattern. First slide is the catalog index, we surface curated open models with a performance profile — speed, token cost, recommended hardware.
[15:33] Rahul Singh: Are those numbers real benchmarks or synthetic?
[15:33] Daniel Lee: They come from our internal benchmark harness — real-ish workloads, we publish seq-len, batch size, and throughput. There's variance vs your queries, that's why we offer a benchmark run with your sample.
[15:34] Elena Gomez: When you say "recommended hardware" is that tied to quantized variants? We need to know if FP16 vs int8 will impact outputs for clinical language.
[15:35] Daniel Lee: Yes, the catalog lists compatible quantization profiles. There's a compatibility matrix per model: columns for q4_0, q8_0, int8, supported kernels (triton/gpu-default/avx), and notes on known regressions. It's not 100% perfect — sometimes the model quality delta appears for low-temp generation, but we track evals.
[15:36] Sofia Martinez: Let me share my screen, Console -> Models -> Catalog. You can filter by language, seq length, and quality tier. For ArborHealth I'd likely filter by medical-domain friendly models and then look at the throughput per 1k tokens at typical batch sizes.
[15:37] [screen share noises]
[15:37] Daniel Lee: Click into a model card — you'll see recent benchmarks: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec on A100 vs T4 equivalents, and a note if we have a verified quantized build.
[15:38] Rahul Singh: Can you run an apples-to-apples: same model, q8 vs fp16 on A100 to see latency and quality?
[15:38] Daniel Lee: Yep, that's what our benchmark runs do. We run both variants, measure perplexity/ROUGE on your eval set if you provide it, and we show cost per 1M tokens.
[15:39] Tom Hsu: How do fallbacks work? If a quantized variant is unavailable in Dedicated pool, will hosted variant be used?
[15:39] Daniel Lee: Policy-based routing — you can prefer Dedicated first, then fallback to compatible hosted variant; we support pinning model versions and automated fallback to similar-capability models.
[15:40] Elena Gomez: Audit logs, can we get token-level tracing, or at least request-level metadata in our SIEM?
[15:40] Daniel Lee: We emit request-level metadata to your chosen log sink in Private/Dedicated modes; hosted API has retention limits but still provides request metadata and aggregated cost. For full token-level trace, Private deployment is the path.
[15:41] Maya Patel: For Dedicated sizing, we have peaks at 20k concurrent requests with typical seq ~150 tokens. What do you recommend?
[15:41] Daniel Lee: We map that to sustained throughput — our sizing worksheet helps calculate required GPU units. For seq=150, 20k concurrent would need heavy pooling; we usually recommend a mix of Dedicated for core flows and Hosted for burst. We'll send a sizing worksheet.
[15:42] Rahul Singh: About the compatibility matrix — does it include memory/KV cache behavior for long contexts? We use KV cache heavily for convo flows.
[15:42] Daniel Lee: The matrix includes notes about KV cache support and estimated memory per slot; also whether the runtime supports efficient eviction and prefix caching. It's in the compatibility CSV we share.
[15:44] Sofia Martinez: I want to highlight Redwood Optimize suggestions — the UI will recommend batching and quant profiles based on your workload, so you get cost reductions without big latency regressions.
[15:44] Rahul Singh: Does Optimize run offline experiments or is it live traffic suggestions?
[15:44] Daniel Lee: Both. It analyzes historical traffic and can run canary experiments on small traffic slices. We also run simulated benchmarks on your sample queries to predict impact.
[15:45] Maya Patel: How reproducible are the benchmark numbers? We need them for procurement justification.
[15:46] Daniel Lee: We provide the raw benchmark spreadsheet and a reproducible harness; if you want, we can run it in your VPC/Dedicated environment so it's end-to-end reproducible.
[15:47] Elena Gomez: Security — SOC2, ISO, KMS, and key rotation policies are critical. Do you support HSM?
[15:48] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC. We'll attach the SOC2 and ISO summaries; for HSM we have integrations documented.
[15:48] Rahul Singh: Any examples of model quality regressions when switching to q8? We worry about hallucinations in clinical contexts.
[15:49] Daniel Lee: We flag models where quantization causes >X% drop in eval metric on domain evals; it's prominent in the compatibility notes. For clinical-critical paths we usually recommend targeted evals and possibly keeping FP16 for those flows.
[15:50] Maya Patel: How long will the benchmark take?
[15:50] Daniel Lee: For 10k queries it's usually a few hours end-to-end; scheduling and queueing might add a day. We'll provision Dedicated test capacity to run it faster.
[15:51] Sofia Martinez: Recap of next steps: We'll send pricing and sizing, Daniel will share the compatibility matrix and benchmark spreadsheet, Rahul will give the 10k sample, and Elena will confirm compliance artifacts.
[15:52] Tom Hsu: Do you have any notes on network egress costs when using Hosted fallback?
[15:52] Sofia Martinez: We include egress estimates in the pricing deck; Dedicated in-region reduces egress. We'll call that out.
[15:53] Maya Patel: Sounds good. If the numbers look reasonable we'll pilot with 2 models and keep critical inference on Dedicated.
[15:54] Daniel Lee: Great — I'll also include suggested canary config for rollouts and an example tracing hook so you can validate latency SLOs.
[15:55] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and set a time for the benchmark sync.
[15:56] Maya Patel: Thanks, talk soon.
[15:56] [call ends]
